entries.name: pydub
entries.noneReason: No deprecation notice, no successor named by the project and no API-compatible maintained fork found on PyPI. Last release 2021-03; it still wraps ffmpeg.

entries.name: defusedxml
entries.noneReason: No replacement exists: it is the standard hardening layer for the stdlib XML parsers, and its own docs say the stdlib is not safe for untrusted XML. Last release 0.7.1 (2021), last commit 2023-10. Likely finished, not dead.

entries.name: ldap3
entries.noneReason: No successor named. Release 2.9.1 is from 2021-07.
entries.notDeadAfterAll: The repository had a commit on 2026-04-18, within 12 months of the check (commit feed).

entries.name: mkdocs-material

successors.name: zensical
successors.reason: Built by the team behind Material for MkDocs. It can read your existing mkdocs.yml; the `classic` theme variant keeps the Material look. Plugins need a compatibility check, so the move is a configuration change plus a plugin review, not a code change.

mapping.note: The README announces end of life on 2027-05-05 and names Zensical as the maintained successor.

entries.notDeadAfterAll: Still shipping: release 9.8.0 on 2026-10-24 and a commit 4 days before the check. The PyPI "Inactive" classifier is true in the sense that end of life is announced (2027-05-05), not that it is abandoned today.

successors.name: python-socks
successors.reason: Maintained SOCKS4/SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy client with sync, asyncio, trio and anyio APIs. The API differs: you build a Proxy from a URL and call connect() instead of using socks.socksocket.

entries.name: cross-env
entries.noneReason: No successor is needed yet: the README says cross-env is "done" (feature complete). The repository was archived on 2025-11-19 after release 10.1.0 (2025-09-29).
entries.notDeadAfterAll: README notice: "cross-env is done as in it does what it does and there is no need for new features" (links issue 257).

successors.name: @babel/plugin-transform-class-properties
successors.reason: The proposal reached the ECMAScript standard, so Babel renamed the plugin. Replace the plugin name in the Babel config; options (`loose`) are unchanged.

successors.name: class fields
successors.reason: Class fields are part of ES2022, so when every target environment supports them the plugin can be removed and the syntax left as it is.

entries.name: @codemirror/lang-python
entries.noneReason: The GitHub repository was archived because the project moved to another Git host; the package continues.
entries.notDeadAfterAll: README: "This repository has moved to code.haverbeke.berlin/codemirror/lang-python". The new host shows commits on 2026-04-15 (page checked).

successors.name: bcryptjs
successors.reason: bcryptjs ships its own type definitions. Delete the @types stub from devDependencies; imports stay the same and the types now come from bcryptjs itself.

mapping.note: The @types stub is deprecated on npm because bcryptjs ships its own types.

entries.name: codemirror
entries.noneReason: The GitHub repository was archived because the project moved to another Git host; the package continues.

successors.name: c8
successors.reason: Uses V8 native coverage instead of source instrumentation, so no instrument step. CLI wraps your command: `c8 node test.js` instead of `istanbul cover`. Reports are the same Istanbul formats.

successors.name: nyc
successors.reason: The deprecation message names nyc. It is the command-line client of the maintained Istanbul libraries, with instrumentation like the old tool; `nyc <cmd>` replaces `istanbul cover <cmd>`.

successors.name: @web/test-runner
successors.reason: Karma is deprecated; its README lists Web Test Runner as a direct alternative for browser tests. Mocha tests run unchanged through the `@web/test-runner-mocha` framework; the config moves from karma.conf.js to web-test-runner.config.mjs.

entries.name: karma-mocha-reporter
entries.noneReason: Only meaningful with Karma, which is deprecated. The way out is leaving Karma (see karma-mocha); the new runner brings its own reporters.

entries.name: process
entries.noneReason: A tiny browser shim of `process.nextTick` that bundlers pull in; no replacement and no deprecation. Last release 2017. Bundlers that target modern browsers can drop the shim, otherwise keep it.

successors.name: pure-rand
successors.reason: Maintained seedable PRNG library (the generator behind fast-check). The API differs: you create a generator from a seed (`prand.xoroshiro128plus(seed)`) and draw numbers through distribution functions, instead of calling a seeded `Math.random`.

successors.name: serve-static
successors.reason: Express/Connect static file middleware maintained by the Express team. Same shape: `serve-static(root, options)` returns a (req, res, next) middleware; options are renamed (`index` instead of `defaultExt`, no built-in directory listing).

mapping.note: sirv, a second candidate, was not offered: no commit for 426 days.

successors.name: expr-eval-fork
successors.reason: Community fork of expr-eval that keeps the API (`Parser.parse(expr).evaluate(scope)`) and fixes the advisories on the original. Update the import and the version pin.

successors.name: unzipper
successors.reason: Maintained unzip library with a streaming `Extract({ path })` API. The call style changes from `await extract(file, { dir })` to piping `fs.createReadStream(file).pipe(unzipper.Extract({ path }))`. Check that it rejects entries that leave the target directory, which is the fault of the open advisories on extract-zip.

successors.name: fetch
successors.reason: Built in to Node 18+ and every browser. Callbacks and streams become promises: `const res = await fetch(url); const data = await res.json()`. Options are renamed (`headers`, `body`, `method`).

successors.name: undici
successors.reason: The HTTP client behind Node fetch, from the Node.js project. Use `undici.request` for a lower-level, faster call with a promise API.

successors.name: ofetch
successors.reason: Fetch wrapper with automatic JSON parsing, retries and base URLs; closest to the convenience of request.

successors.name: ky
successors.reason: Small fetch wrapper with retries, hooks and JSON helpers.

successors.name: unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase
successors.reason: The standard library has async test cases since Python 3.8: subclass IsolatedAsyncioTestCase and write `async def test_...`. No extra package; asynctest's coroutine mocks become `unittest.mock.AsyncMock`.

successors.name: python-box
successors.reason: Dictionary with attribute access that is maintained; `Box(d)` replaces `AttrDict(d)`. Methods differ in names (`to_dict()`), and nested lists are converted too.

successors.name: types.SimpleNamespace
successors.reason: For flat data the standard library has attribute access: `SimpleNamespace(**d)`. It is not a dict and does not nest.

mapping.note: PyPI marks it Development Status 7 Inactive. attrdict3, the usual fork, is itself archived (2026-01-14) and munch has had no commit for 1221 days, so neither is offered.

successors.name: python-box
successors.reason: Dictionary with attribute access that is maintained; `Box(d)` replaces `AttrDict(d)`.

mapping.note: Fork of attrdict; archived on GitHub 2026-01-14, last release 2022-04.

successors.name: codecov-cli
successors.reason: The new Codecov uploader, from the Codecov team. The command changes from `codecov` to `codecovcli upload-process` (token via CODECOV_TOKEN).

mapping.note: The README deprecates this uploader and links a migration guide to the new Codecov CLI.

successors.name: pydoclint
successors.reason: Python docstring linter that checks the arguments, returns, yields and raises sections against the signature, which is the job darglint did. It runs standalone or as a flake8 plugin; rule codes change from DAR to DOC.

entries.name: g2p-en
entries.noneReason: No successor named; a drop-in is not known. Phoneme libraries exist but have different outputs and dictionaries.

entries.name: gntp
entries.noneReason: Growl notification client; no maintained drop-in found. The Apprise library can send Growl notifications but is a different API.

entries.name: jieba
entries.noneReason: No successor named by the project; maintained Chinese segmenters exist but have different APIs and outputs.

successors.name: types-lxml
successors.reason: The README says lxml-stubs is not maintained and was superseded by types-lxml, a more complete, externally maintained stub package. Install types-lxml and remove lxml-stubs; type checkers pick it up with no code change.

entries.name: mutatormath
entries.noneReason: Font-design library; no successor named and no replacement found.

successors.name: nest-asyncio2
successors.reason: Maintained fork with the same `nest_asyncio.apply()` call; change the import to `nest_asyncio2`.

mapping.note: The GitHub repository was archived on 2024-03-06; the original author is no longer working on it.

entries.name: ntplib
entries.noneReason: No successor named. The repository had a commit in 2024-04.

successors.name: pydot
successors.reason: pydotplus began as a fork of pydot; pydot is maintained again and offers the same `graph_from_dot_data` and `write_png` style calls. Change the import from pydotplus to pydot.

entries.name: pyserial
entries.noneReason: No successor named. The 3.5 release is from 2020-11.
entries.notDeadAfterAll: The repository had a commit on 2026-02-27, within 12 months of the check (commit feed).

successors.name: pytest-env
successors.reason: Maintained pytest plugin that sets environment variables from pytest configuration and can load them from `.env` files. The `env_files` setting keeps its name but moves into the `[tool.pytest_env]` table (see its README); `--envfile` selects a file on the command line.

successors.name: pytest
successors.reason: pytest 9.0 and later has built-in support for subtests ("Support for subtests has been added" in the 9.0.0 changelog), so the plugin is not needed. Raise the pytest pin to 9 or newer and use the `subtests` fixture.

successors.name: unittest.TestCase.subTest
successors.reason: The standard library `subTest` context manager covers the same need for unittest-style classes.

mapping.note: Archived on 2025-11-11, the week pytest 9.0.0 (2025-11-05) added subtests to pytest itself.

entries.name: python-terraform
entries.noneReason: Thin wrapper over the terraform command; no maintained fork found. Calling `subprocess.run(["terraform", ...])` is the plain alternative.

successors.name: myst-parser
successors.reason: The README says recommonmark is deprecated and recommends MyST. MyST-Parser reads CommonMark plus extensions for Sphinx; set `extensions = ["myst_parser"]` instead of the recommonmark parser and rename the config keys.

entries.name: reverse-geocoder
entries.noneReason: Offline reverse geocoder, last release 2016; no successor named and no drop-in found.

entries.name: seqeval
entries.noneReason: No successor named. The repository had a commit in 2024-08, the last release is from 2020-10.

entries.name: soynlp
entries.noneReason: Korean NLP toolkit, last release 2019; no successor named.

successors.name: sphinx-polyversion
successors.reason: Builds several versions of a Sphinx site and merges them into one website (its PyPI summary), the job sphinx-multiversion did. It is driven by a build script instead of a Sphinx extension, so the setup is rewritten.

successors.name: unicodedata
successors.reason: The package describes itself as an alternative to the standard library `unicodedata`. The stdlib covers category and name lookups for the Unicode version bundled with your Python; the package existed to offer newer Unicode data and extra fields (block, script).

successors.name: pytest-postgresql
successors.reason: Maintained pytest plugin that starts a throwaway PostgreSQL server for tests. It exposes fixtures instead of a context manager, so tests change to take a `postgresql` fixture.

successors.name: ua-parser
successors.reason: user-agents is a convenience layer over the ua-parser data. ua-parser is maintained and returns browser, OS and device; helpers such as `is_mobile` are not included and become a check on the device family.

successors.reason: The proposal is part of ES2018, so Babel renamed the plugin; change the name in the Babel config.

successors.name: spread syntax

successors.name: @babel/plugin-transform-optional-chaining
successors.reason: The proposal is part of ES2020, so Babel renamed the plugin; change the name in the Babel config.

successors.name: optional chaining
successors.reason: Optional chaining (`a?.b`) is standard JavaScript; when all targets support it the plugin can go.

entries.name: add-cors-to-couchdb

successors.name: tinybench
successors.reason: Small maintained benchmark runner with statistics. A suite is `new Bench()` plus `bench.add(name, fn)` and `await bench.run()` instead of `new Benchmark.Suite()` and events.

mapping.note: mitata, a second candidate, was not offered: no commit for 625 days.

entries.name: browserify-incremental
entries.noneReason: Plugin for Browserify, which is legacy; no successor named. Moving to a bundler that is incremental by default (esbuild, Vite) is a build change, not a swap.

entries.name: chai-enzyme
entries.noneReason: Assertions for enzyme wrappers; it goes away with enzyme. With React Testing Library the DOM assertions come from @testing-library/jest-dom or chai-dom, a different style.

entries.name: circular-dependency-plugin
entries.noneReason: Webpack plugin; no successor named. Standalone checkers such as madge exist but work outside the webpack build.

entries.name: codecov

entries.name: codecov.io
entries.noneReason: Old LCOV poster for Codecov (2015). The way out is the current Codecov uploader (CLI or GitHub Action), not an npm package.

successors.name: which
successors.reason: Maintained by the npm team: `which.sync(cmd, { nothrow: true })` returns the path or null, where command-exists returned a boolean.

successors.name: cpy-cli
successors.reason: Command line copy with glob patterns and a maintained codebase: `cpy "src/**/*.html" dist` replaces `copyfiles -u 1 "src/**/*.html" dist` (folder flattening uses `--cwd`).

successors.name: fs.cp
successors.reason: For copying one folder tree without globs, Node 16.7+ has `fs.cp(src, dest, { recursive: true })`.

successors.name: coveralls-next
successors.reason: The README says the project is no longer maintained and names coveralls-next as the recommended fork. Same command: `coveralls-next` reads LCOV from stdin like `coveralls`.

entries.name: curl-amd
entries.noneReason: AMD module loader (2014). The way out is native ES modules and a bundler, a rewrite, not a swap.

entries.name: cz-conventional-changelog
entries.noneReason: Commitizen adapter; no successor named. The repository had a commit in 2024-09.

successors.name: Promise.all
successors.reason: Run tasks together with `await Promise.all(tasks.map((t) => t()))`; callbacks become promises. For a concurrency limit use `p-limit`.

successors.name: p-limit
successors.reason: Adds a concurrency limit to promise-returning tasks: `const limit = pLimit(n)` replaces `d3.queue(n)`.

entries.name: dekko
entries.noneReason: File layout assertion helper, last release 2016; no successor found.

successors.name: util.promisify
successors.reason: Node turns a callback-style function into a promise function with `util.promisify(fn)`. Same idea, built in.

successors.name: detect-port
successors.reason: detect-port-alt is a fork of detect-port made for Create React App; the original is maintained. Same call `detectPort(port)` returning a promise; change the package name.

successors.name: diff-match-patch-es
successors.reason: ESM and TypeScript rewrite of diff-match-patch whose README has a migration section from this exact npm package: the class and default export are gone, functions are camelCase (`diff(a, b)` instead of `dmp.diff_main(a, b)`) and options such as `Diff_Timeout` become an options object.

entries.name: docdown
entries.noneReason: jsdoc-to-markdown, the usual replacement, failed the aliveness check (no commit for 396 days), so it is not offered. No other drop-in found.

entries.name: double-ended-queue
entries.noneReason: denque, the usual replacement, failed the aliveness check (repository archived, no commit for 1569 days), so it is not offered. No other drop-in found; a plain Array with push/shift is the fallback for small queues.

successors.name: @testing-library/react
successors.reason: Tests query the rendered DOM by role and text instead of component internals (`render`, `screen.getByRole`), so enzyme's `shallow` and `mount` tests are rewritten, not renamed. It supports current React versions.

successors.name: eslint-config-airbnb-extended
successors.reason: The README of the archived project lists it as the alternative (shared for discoverability, not a personal recommendation). It is a flat-config rewrite, so the ESLint config file changes shape.

successors.name: @babel/eslint-plugin
successors.reason: The README says eslint-plugin-babel is now @babel/eslint-plugin and lives in the Babel monorepo. Rename the plugin in the ESLint config (`babel/` rules become `@babel/` rules).

successors.name: @eslint/markdown
successors.reason: The registry message says to use @eslint/markdown, the official ESLint plugin; it targets flat config and also lints the Markdown itself.

successors.name: @stylistic/eslint-plugin
successors.reason: Provides `@stylistic/no-mixed-operators`, the maintained home of the stylistic rule (the core rule has no autofix). Rename the rule in the ESLint config.

successors.name: eslint-plugin-n
successors.reason: The README says the project is no longer maintained and points to eslint-community/eslint-plugin-n, a fork that keeps the rules. Rename `node/` rules to `n/` in the ESLint config.

successors.name: ECMAScript modules in Node
successors.reason: Node runs ES modules natively (`"type": "module"` or `.mjs`), and newer releases can `require()` them. Remove the `-r esm` flag and convert import specifiers to include file extensions.

entries.name: express-pouchdb
entries.noneReason: Part of pouchdb-server; no successor named. The repository had a commit in 2025-08, the release is from 2019.

successors.name: util.isDeepStrictEqual
successors.reason: In Node, `util.isDeepStrictEqual(a, b)` does a strict deep comparison. It is not available in browsers, and it compares `NaN` and prototypes strictly, which differs from fast-deep-equal in edge cases.

entries.name: find-requires
entries.noneReason: No successor named; scanning `require()` calls is also done by bundler plugins.

entries.name: foreach-cli
entries.noneReason: No successor named and no drop-in found.

entries.name: grunt-compare-size
entries.noneReason: Grunt plugin; no successor named.

entries.name: grunt-contrib-watch
entries.noneReason: Grunt plugin (last release 2018). The way out is leaving Grunt for npm scripts and a file watcher; no drop-in plugin named.

entries.name: grunt-exec
entries.noneReason: Grunt plugin; no successor named.

entries.name: gulp-less
entries.noneReason: Gulp plugin (last release 2021); no successor named.

successors.name: CompressionStream
successors.reason: Browsers and Node 18+ compress with the Compression Streams API: `new CompressionStream("gzip")`. It is stream based and asynchronous, where gzip-js returned arrays synchronously.

successors.name: zlib.gzipSync
successors.reason: In Node only, `zlib.gzipSync(buffer)` keeps the synchronous call style.

entries.name: headr
entries.noneReason: No successor named.

successors.name: identity-obj-proxy
successors.reason: The package is one Proxy that returns each key as its own name, so the project can own it as a stub file mapped with Jest `moduleNameMapper` (about 10 lines): `new Proxy({}, { get: (_, key) => (key === "__esModule" ? false : key) })`.

entries.name: is-git-clean
entries.noneReason: Last release 2016; no successor named. It runs `git status --porcelain`, which a project can call directly.

entries.name: ismobilejs
entries.noneReason: No successor named.
entries.notDeadAfterAll: The repository had a commit 38 days before the check (commit feed) and the README documents a recent migration note; the last npm release is from 2020-04.

successors.name: fetch
successors.reason: Node 18+ and all browsers have a global fetch, which is all this package polyfilled. Remove the import.

successors.name: ofetch
successors.reason: If a convenience layer is wanted: a fetch wrapper with JSON handling and retries.

successors.name: Intl.Collator
successors.reason: Natural ordering is built in: `array.sort(new Intl.Collator(undefined, { numeric: true }).compare)` or `a.localeCompare(b, undefined, { numeric: true })`. Case and accent handling follow the locale.

entries.name: js-reporters
entries.noneReason: QUnit includes this reporter interface natively since 2.2 (README); no separate successor is needed for QUnit users.

successors.name: eslint
successors.reason: The registry message says JSCS merged with ESLint. Style rules become ESLint rules (and formatting rules move to a formatter such as Prettier); .jscsrc is rewritten as an ESLint config.

entries.noneReason: No successor named.

successors.name: vitest
successors.reason: Named in the Karma README as a Node-based alternative; with its browser mode it can run tests in a real browser.

entries.name: karma-webdriver-launcher
entries.noneReason: A Karma launcher for remote WebDriver browsers (archived 2026-04-19). Karma is deprecated; the way out is a runner with its own browser launcher (see karma-cli).

successors.name: level-transcoder
successors.reason: The registry message and README say level-codec was superseded by level-transcoder. It is the encoding layer of abstract-level; encodings are named strings (`utf8`, `json`) instead of codec objects.

entries.name: level-write-stream
entries.noneReason: Last release 2014; no successor named.

successors.name: classic-level
successors.reason: The registry message says leveldown was superseded by classic-level: the same LevelDB binding as an abstract-level database. `level(location)` or `new ClassicLevel(location)` replaces `levelup(leveldown(location))`.

successors.name: abstract-level
successors.reason: The registry message says levelup was superseded by abstract-level. Databases are classes with promise APIs (`await db.put(k, v)`) and their own iterators, instead of a levelup wrapper over a down-store.

entries.name: load-json-file

successors.name: fs.readFile + JSON.parse
successors.reason: Reading JSON takes one line with Node built-ins: `JSON.parse(await fs.readFile(path, "utf8"))`. Error messages with the file name are lost.

entries.notDeadAfterAll: The repository had a commit 46 days before the check (commit feed); the 7.0.1 release is from 2021-09.

successors.name: browser-level
successors.reason: The abstract-level family has a browser database (IndexedDB) in place of localStorage-backed leveldown. The store changes from localStorage to IndexedDB and the API becomes the abstract-level API.

entries.name: lodash-doc-globals

entries.name: ltgt

entries.noneReason: No successor named.

entries.name: material-colors

successors.name: median
successors.reason: Computing a median is a few lines the project can own: sort a copy of the array and take the middle value (the mean of the two middle values for an even count).

successors.name: memory-level
successors.reason: The registry message says memdown was superseded by memory-level, an in-memory abstract-level database. `new MemoryLevel()` replaces `memdown()`.

successors.name: c8
successors.reason: Produces LCOV from V8 coverage for any test command: `c8 --reporter=lcov mocha`. Coverage is collected by c8, not by a Mocha reporter, so the reporter option is removed.

successors.name: node:test mock timers
successors.reason: The Node test runner can set a fake clock: `mock.timers.enable({ apis: ["Date"] })` and `mock.timers.setTime(ms)` replace `MockDate.set(ms)`.

successors.name: vitest
successors.reason: With Vitest, `vi.useFakeTimers()` and `vi.setSystemTime(date)` replace `MockDate.set(date)`.

entries.name: mustache
entries.noneReason: No deprecation or successor; release 4.2.0 (2021-03) is the latest and the repository had its last commit in 2023-01. Likely finished.

successors.name: fs.cp
successors.reason: Node 16.7+ copies directories recursively with `fs.cp(src, dest, { recursive: true })` and a promise form `fs.promises.cp`. The callback becomes a promise; `filter` replaces ncp's filter option.

successors.reason: The README says node-loader is deprecated in favour of the nodejs-addons example in webpack itself, which loads .node addons with a built-in asset rule. The loader entry in the webpack config is replaced by that rule.

successors.name: npm-run-all2
successors.reason: A maintained fork with the same commands (`run-s`, `run-p`, `npm-run-all`); change the package name only.

successors.name: concurrently
successors.reason: Runs commands in parallel with prefixed output; `concurrently "a" "b"` replaces `run-p a b`.

successors.name: wireit
successors.reason: Adds dependency graphs and caching to npm scripts; a bigger change, defined in package.json.

entries.name: numericjs
entries.noneReason: Numerical library, last release 2016; no successor named.

entries.notDeadAfterAll: README: "This repository has moved to code.haverbeke.berlin/marijn/orderedmap".

successors.name: bowser
successors.reason: Maintained user agent parser: `Bowser.parse(navigator.userAgent)` returns browser, OS and platform objects with other field names than platform.js's `platform.name`, `platform.os`.

entries.name: pluralize
entries.noneReason: No deprecation or successor. The repository moved to the `plurals` organisation and the last commit was in 2023-12.

entries.name: postcss-flexbugs-fixes

entries.name: progress
entries.noneReason: The usual replacement, cli-progress, failed the aliveness check (no commit since 2023-03), so it is not offered. No other drop-in found.

entries.name: prop-types
entries.noneReason: No package replaces it. React 19 removed propTypes checks for function components (React 19 upgrade guide); the way out is static types (TypeScript) or deleting the checks. See https://react.dev/blog/2024/04/25/react-19-upgrade-guide ("Removed: propTypes and defaultProps for functions").

successors.name: react-colorful
successors.reason: Small, maintained React color picker. Components are `HexColorPicker` and friends with `color` and `onChange`; the Sketch/Chrome/Photoshop styles of react-color are not included.

successors.name: @rollup/plugin-replace
successors.reason: The registry message says the plugin moved to @rollup/plugin-replace. Change the import; `preventAssignment: true` is advised in the new plugin.

successors.name: rollup-plugin-sourcemaps2

successors.name: chai
successors.reason: Chai has a `should` interface (`chai.should()`) with a very similar chained syntax, and a maintained codebase; matchers are renamed in places.

entries.name: spark-md5
entries.noneReason: Browser MD5 has no built-in (Web Crypto has no MD5). hash-wasm, the usual replacement, failed the aliveness check (no commit for 714 days), so it is not offered. If the hash is not required to be MD5, crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256") is built in.

entries.name: spinnies
entries.noneReason: Multi-spinner CLI helper; no successor named.

successors.name: node:stream/promises
successors.reason: The registry message and README point to node:stream/promises and node:stream/consumers (Node 16+). `await buffer(stream)` or `await text(stream)` replaces `streamToPromise(stream)`, and `await finished(stream)` replaces it for writables.

successors.name: webpack
successors.reason: The README says style-loader is deprecated because webpack now injects CSS itself; it links a native CSS guide and a migration guide. The loader chain changes to webpack's built-in CSS handling.

entries.name: sylvester
entries.noneReason: Matrix library, last release 2012; no successor named.

entries.name: throw-max-listeners-error
entries.noneReason: Last release 2015; no successor named.

successors.name: EventTarget
successors.reason: Node 15+ and browsers have `EventTarget` and `CustomEvent`: `target.addEventListener(name, fn)` and `target.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent(name, { detail }))` replace `on` and `emit` (data moves to `event.detail`).

entries.name: tree-kill
entries.noneReason: No successor named and no deprecation; the package is small and its job (kill a process tree) has no built-in. Likely finished.

successors.name: crypto.randomUUID
successors.reason: A v4 UUID is built in to Node 14.17+ and every browser: `crypto.randomUUID()` replaces `uuid()`.

successors.name: uuid
successors.reason: The `uuid` package covers every UUID version if more than v4 is needed; `v4()` replaces `uuid()`.

successors.name: vitest
successors.reason: Vitest has a built-in `github-actions` reporter (listed in its reporters guide), so the extra reporter can be removed: `reporters: ["default", "github-actions"]`.

entries.name: vue-toastification
entries.noneReason: No successor named. Vue 3 users are told to take the 2.x line, which exists only as release candidates (2.0.0-rc.5, 2021-10) and a dev build (2022-01); the repository has had no commit since 2022-02.

entries.name: vuvuzela
entries.noneReason: No successor named; native JSON works except for very deep nesting.

successors.name: webdriverio
successors.reason: The README says to remove the service and its entry in the WebdriverIO config when using WebdriverIO 8.14 or newer: the runner now manages geckodriver itself. Nothing replaces it in code.

successors.name: @xterm/addon-web-links
successors.reason: The registry message says to move to @xterm/addon-web-links (xterm.js moved to the @xterm scope together with @xterm/xterm). Change the import; the `WebLinksAddon` API is unchanged.

entries.name: yalc
entries.noneReason: No successor named. `npm link` and workspaces cover similar needs differently.

successors.name: timers/promises.setTimeout
successors.reason: Node 15+ has a promise `setTimeout` in node:timers/promises: `await setTimeout(ms)`. In a browser, `new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms))` is the same in one line.
